content:
Last week, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing its former employees of stealing trade secrets "for the benefit of OpenAI."

During the litigation process, Apple is reported to have directly contacted several former employees who currently work at OpenAI.

According to the Financial Times, Apple has issued evidence preservation letters to approximately 40 former employees.

An evidence preservation letter is a formal written notice sent to an individual or organization, requiring them to preserve documents, records, and other evidence related to a legal dispute. Such letters typically specify what needs to be preserved.

This move stems from Apple's suspicion that the theft of trade secrets may extend beyond the individuals named in last week's initial lawsuit.

In short, Apple's lawsuit names OpenAI and io Products, along with former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan, as defendants.

You can read more details about Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI here:

  • Apple sues OpenAI, accusing former employees of stealing trade secrets
  • An email mishap derailed pre-lawsuit negotiations between Apple and OpenAI
  • Apple's lawsuit filings reveal how many former employees it currently has working at OpenAI
  • OpenAI says it has seen no evidence to support Apple's allegations of trade secret theft
  • OpenAI's hardware launch timeline remains unchanged after Apple's lawsuit

You can read the full copy of Apple's initial lawsuit filings here.
